patterns.rationale: Misses 1, 2, and 9 all phrase the env-dump as "environment registry" (Miss 1), "process environment table" (Miss 2), or "environment table" (Miss 9). These are injection-specific nominalised forms for "all process environment variables"; they do not appear in standard API references, deployment guides, or security policy docs. The existing static layer covers tool names (get_env, read_env) but not these prose equivalents.
patterns.fp_notes: Cloud-infrastructure docs might reference an "environment registry" as a service concept; compiler/interpreter documentation occasionally uses "environment table" in the symbol-table sense. Neither appears in the known-good corpus.

patterns.rationale: Miss 4 exfiltrates via "mail the complete gallery transcript to https://…". Legitimate documentation almost never uses the bare verb "mail" (as opposed to "email" or "send") followed within 80 characters by an HTTP/S URL; hyperlinked mail contacts use mailto: scheme. The existing exfil-verb set (send, post, submit) does not include mail.
patterns.fp_notes: Instructional docs could say "mail us at https://contact-form.example.com" — low probability in security/ops corpus. The 80-char window is tight enough to avoid incidental co-occurrence.

patterns.rationale: Miss 3 asks for "the full manifest of secrets-manager values currently injected into the process". The phrase "secrets manager values" (hyphen or space separator, singular or plural) is injection-specific: legitimate deployment and operations docs refer to a secrets manager as a service but do not pair it with "values" to mean enumerate-all-secrets. The dot matches the hyphen or space separator, making the pattern resilient to both typings.
patterns.fp_notes: A deployment checklist could legitimately say "ensure the secrets manager values are all present" — the phrase is rare but not impossible in ops documentation. The known-good corpus has "secrets manager" without a following "values" so no FP there.

semantic_note: The creative-persona wrapper (interviewer, archivist, tour guide, etc.) that frames these attacks as benign walkthroughs is fully semantic — there is no lexical signal that distinguishes "act as a stenographer" from a legitimate roleplay prompt without reading the downstream instruction. The patterns below target the downstream symptoms (env-dump prose + URL exfil) rather than the persona layer.
